name: Raton Pass Camp & Cafe
note: Seasonal (Mar-Nov) big-rig-friendly RV park at I-25 Exit 460 atop Raton Pass (~7,500 ft) near the CO border: 30 level pull-through/back-in full-hookup sites with true 50-amp, showers, laundry, free WiFi. On-site cafe no longer operating. Reservable online/by phone. --Claude

name: Sky Mountain Resort RV Park
note: Seasonal (approx May 15-Oct 15) RV park in a cottonwood/spruce grove along the Rio Chama at Chama; full hookups (50/30/20), big-rig sites to 60 ft, in-floor-heated bathhouse, laundry, enclosed dog park. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Weathers RV Park
note: Seasonal (May-Oct) 25-site commercial RV park ~1 mi east of Eagle Nest on US-64; full hookups with 30/50-amp, WiFi/laundry/game room, near Eagle Nest Lake trout fishing. Reservable. --Claude

name: Circle Cross RV Park
note: Private 6-acre park at the edge of Lincoln NF in Timberon (Sacramento Mtns, ~7,000 ft); 40 full-hookup pull-through sites, 20/30/50-amp, bathhouse/laundry, open ~May-Sept, abundant elk/deer/turkey. --Claude

name: C.M. Wilson Conservation Area
note: Lower Thames Valley Conservation Authority campground 8.5 km south of Chatham, set in Carolinian forest around a man-made lake; ~100 drive-in sites with hydro, hydro+water or unserviced, serviced washrooms with showers and on-site dump; open Victoria Day to Thanksgiving. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Bronte Creek Provincial Park
note: Ontario Parks park on the Bronte Creek tableland near Oakville; ~149 drive-in car-camping sites, 145 electric, accommodates 'tents to large RVs'; large outdoor pool and comfort stations. Open May–Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Earl Rowe Provincial Park
note: Ontario Parks car-camping park on the Boyne River reservoir near Alliston. Riverside campground (Heydon Way/Blue Heron electrical, Salmon Run/Rabbit Loop tent-only) open May-Oct and Westside campground (Fletcher's Field electrical, Boyne Meadow, Trillium Woods, Meadowbrook) June-Sept - tents to large RVs. Beach and fish ladder. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Farran Park Campground
note: St. Lawrence Parks Commission (Ontario government) campground on a St. Lawrence River peninsula at Ingleside; 215+ sites incl full 3-service, electric-only and pull-through big-rig sites, beach, boat launch; open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Lake Superior Provincial Park - Rabbit Blanket Lake Campground
note: Rabbit Blanket Lake Campground: 205 car-camping sites incl 58 electric and 53 RV pull-through; drive-in RV campground on Rabbit Blanket Lake off Hwy 17, N of Wawa. Trailer dump station; open mid-May to late Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Ivanhoe Lake Provincial Park
note: Drive-in car campground on Ivanhoe Lake between Chapleau and Timmins: 104 car-camping sites, 63 electrical, 37 pull-through; two comfort stations with showers, vault privies, trailer dump/fill station, laundromat. Season mid-May to late Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Nagagamisis Provincial Park
note: Drive-in car campground on the fine sandy shore of Nagagamisis Lake near Hornepayne: 107 car-camping sites (Shaganash and Bedwash campgrounds), 19 pull-through, non-electric; boat launch, fish-cleaning station, trailer dump station, laundromat. Season mid-May to late Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Kettle Lakes Provincial Park
note: Drive-in car campground set among 22 spring-fed kettle lakes ~35 km east of Timmins: 137 car-camping sites, 93 electrical; comfort stations, trailer dump station. Season mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Esker Lakes Provincial Park
note: Family-oriented drive-in car campground in the Esker Lakes area NE of Kirkland Lake: 103 car-camping sites, 65 electrical, no pull-throughs; on Panagapka Lake. Season mid-May to late Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Pakwash Provincial Park
note: Small drive-in car campground on the east shore of Pakwash Lake, ~20 km NW of Ear Falls: 69 car-camping sites, 26 electrical, 20 pull-through; sandy beach, boat launch, trailer dump station, laundromat. A few sites sit apart from the main campground with their own beachfront. Season mid-May to mid-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Warsaw Caves Conservation Area
note: 52 unserviced drive-in campsites in a wooded setting (color groups: Pink 1-22, Yellow 23-52); no electric/water/sewer. Firsthand review reports large, level, well-packed gravel pads easily fitting a 28-ft RV (online length filter is unreliable). Accessible comfort station with showers/laundry. Indian River valley (canoe/kayak, caves, trails). Season May-Oct; reservable online. Operated by Otonabee Region Conservation Authority. --Claude

name: Dalewood Conservation Area
note: Kettle Creek CA campground beside Dalewood Reservoir north of St. Thomas; ~200+ serviced (15/30-amp, some 45-amp pull-through) plus unserviced sites, open May-Sept, transient + seasonal. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Holiday Beach Conservation Area
note: Essex Region CA campground on Lake Erie (sandy beach, Big Creek marsh) near Amherstburg; ~15 paved back-in RV sites, 20/50-amp metered, water, comfort station/showers, max ~30 ft, no tents; seasonal (~Apr-Oct). Reservable online. --Claude

name: Big Bend Conservation Area
note: Lower Thames Valley CA campground within a Thames River meander at Morpeth; 48 sites incl. 6 electric (4x30-amp, 2x15-amp w/ water), unserviced traditional sites + 10 backcountry riverfront sites; no dump station; open Victoria Day-Thanksgiving. Reservable online + FCFS. --Claude

name: Lake Whittaker Conservation Area
note: Kettle Creek Conservation Authority campground on a 26-acre spring-fed lake; serviced (15/30-amp) and unserviced drive-in sites in ravine and lakeshore loops, plus a beach, pool and watercraft rentals. Open May-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Springwater Conservation Area
note: Catfish Creek Conservation Authority campground; full-service campground with serviced trailer lots and tent sites, washrooms/showers, a camp store, and a sandy beach on a spring-fed reservoir (swimming, non-motorized boating, fishing). Open May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Cathcart Park & Campground
note: Municipal campground operated by the Township of St. Clair on the bank of the St. Clair River; ~84 drive-in sites with gravel pads, water and hydro, plus a playground, boat launch, pavilion and an island reached by a walking bridge. Open May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Fifty Point Conservation Area
note: Hamilton Conservation Authority campground on the south shore of Lake Ontario in Winona/Stoney Creek; 70 fully serviced (sewer/hydro/water) drive-in sites, comfort station with showers and laundry, and a 330-slip marina with double boat launch. Open Apr-Nov. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Laurel Creek Conservation Area
note: Grand River Conservation Authority campground on the Laurel Creek Reservoir in Waterloo. 114 sites (76 serviced with electric+water, 38 unserviced), flush toilets/showers, dump station; season ~mid-May to late Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Albion Hills Conservation Park and Campground
note: Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) campground in the hills of Caledon on the Humber River. 234 serviced and unserviced sites including pull-throughs for RVs; pool/splashpad, dump station, laundry; season ~May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Pinehurst Lake Conservation Area
note: Grand River Conservation Authority campground around a 9-hectare kettle lake in Carolinian forest north of Paris/Ayr. 233 sites (169 with hydro+water, 64 unserviced) across camping Areas 1-4; sandy beach, non-motorized boating; season May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Long Beach Conservation Area
note: Niagara Peninsula Conservation Authority campground on a sandy Lake Erie beach in Wainfleet. ~225 sites with 30-amp electric+water plus dry sites (transient and seasonal); season ~mid-May to late Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Pittock Conservation Area
note: Upper Thames River Conservation Authority campground on the north shore of Pittock Lake reservoir, Woodstock. ~248 treed sites (230 with electricity) in Lakeview/Maple Crest/Trailside (pool) sections; overnight camping opened 2024; season May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Chippawa Creek Conservation Area
note: Niagara Peninsula Conservation Authority campground on the Welland River at Dils Lake reservoir. 156 sites, gravel pads, max RV length 32 ft, non-serviced and 15A/30A (incl premium); two accessible fishing piers, swimming, paddling, playground. Open May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Wesley Acres Retreat Centre & Campground
note: Christian family campground on a West Lake peninsula in Prince Edward County (near Sandbanks). Open to the public with short-term RV sites and tent sites (RV hookups, dump station) plus cabins/motel rooms; beach, boat launch, restaurant. Open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Saugeen Bluffs Conservation Area
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: Saugeen Valley Conservation Authority campground 4 km north of Paisley by the Saugeen River, with 102 sites with 30-amp power and 79 without, plus a separate horse-camping loop; it is open from late April to mid-October. --Claude

name: Brucedale Conservation Area
note: Saugeen Valley CA campground on the Lake Huron shore between Port Elgin and Kincardine; 52 rustic sites in cedar woodland, mostly seasonal with some transient sites, sand beach. Open late April to Thanksgiving. Book by phone/email (no online reservations). --Claude

name: Memorial Park Campground

season.note: Mid-May to Thanksgiving weekend, says the town; its CampLife description says late October.

season_source: https://www.meaford.ca/memorial-park/ ('Open from mid-May until Thanksgiving weekend each year'), read 2026-10-14; https://www.camplife.com/950/reservation/step1 (description: 'The campground is open mid May until the late October.'; camplife_tier_2026-10-14.jsonl), read 2026-10-14
note: Municipality of Meaford campground in Memorial Park, on 468 m of Georgian Bay shoreline: 18 waterfront and 125 forest sites, with full service or water and hydro only, a dump station, public washrooms, a snack shack, two pavilions, playgrounds, an 18-hole mini golf course, woodland trails and a beach with a section for dogs. --Claude

name: Riverside-Cedar Campground
note: Largest St. Lawrence Parks Commission campground (300+ sites) on the St. Lawrence River near Upper Canada Village, Morrisburg; includes 29 premium waterfront sites, regular and electric-only sites, and RV sites with water & 15A/30A, plus dump station, showers and boat launch. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: St. Lawrence Park
note: City of Brockville municipal park on the St. Lawrence River; serviced (15-amp electrical + water) and non-serviced drive-in sites, sandy supervised beach, dump station (no sewer hookups); open Victoria Day to Labour Day, 21-day max stay. Accepts RVs, trailers and camper vans. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Booster Park Campground
note: Municipality of Marmora and Lake park on Crowe Lake; 60 sites including 30 full-hookup and 10 electric/water, 6 pull-throughs, dump station, boat ramp, swimming, playground; open May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Thessalon Lakeside Park Campground
note: Town of Thessalon park beside Lakeside Beach on Lake Huron (North Channel); 33 grass sites to 70 ft, 30-amp, 4 full-hookup + 29 water/electric; open Victoria Day weekend to Thanksgiving. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Westview Park
note: City of Elliot Lake park on Horne (Westview) Lake; 18 grass full-hookup sites, 30-amp, RVs to 40 ft, boat launch, no tents; open May-Oct, nightly rates. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Anicinabe RV Park & Campground
note: Indigenous-owned RV park (run by a Kenora development corp) on Lake of the Woods (Middle Lake); 30A/15A full-service, water/electric, and unserviced sites (back-in/pull-in, no pull-through), boat launch, laundry, WiFi, playground. Open May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Penn Lake Park Campground
note: Town of Marathon municipal campground on Penn Lake; 16 serviced sites (30/15A) plus 2 full-hookup sites (50/30/15A, sewer/water) and 9 unserviced tent sites, comfort station with showers/laundry, beach, hiking trail. Open seasonally. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Poplar Lodge Park
note: Municipality of Greenstone campground on Lake Nipigon east of Beardmore; 97 sites, 45 with electric/water (30A) fitting big rigs, comfort station, vault toilets, pump-out, sandy beach, shoreline trail. Nightly transient camping (from ~$41); seasonal sites allotted by annual draw. Open mid-May to early Sep. --Claude

name: Prospect Hill Campground
note: Family campground on Fish Creek near Granton; 168 sites (~28 tent-only, rest RV) with 30-amp electric + water hookups, showers, laundry, pool, playground; big grassy sites. Open May-October. Reservable online. --Claude

name: South Side Landing Marina and RV Park
note: Small marina + RV park on the Erieau peninsula between Rondeau Bay and Lake Erie; ~15-17 transient RV sites with hydro & water hookups, boat ramp. Book by phone/email (no online reservation system). Seasonal operation. --Claude

name: Shelter Valley Campground
note: 40+ acre park in the Maitland River valley between Goderich and Clinton; ~178 spaces, mainly seasonal with transient overnight pull-thru and big-rig sites, hookups, solar-heated pool, dump station. Open May-October. Reservable. --Claude

name: MacKenzie Tent & Trailer Park
note: Lakeside park at Kintail on Lake Huron, ~21 km north of Goderich; 124 grass sites offering overnight sites (30-amp full-service, 15-amp with water, and no-service) plus weekly/seasonal, with beach access. Open May-September. Reservations preferred. --Claude

name: Providence Bay Tent & Trailer Park
note: Large campground (~250 sites) at Providence Bay on the Lake Huron south shore of Manitoulin Island; serviced 20/30-amp + water and unserviced sites, pull-throughs, dump station, laundry, store; daily/weekly/seasonal. Open May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Breakwater Park Campground at Meldrum Bay
note: Small 17-site campground on a natural point at Meldrum Bay, far west end of Manitoulin Island; 14 sites with hydro, 12 also with water; adjacent Meldrum Bay Marina with boat launch, showers, laundry. Daily/weekly/seasonal, open ~May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Roth Park Family Campground
season_source: https://www.rothparkfamilycampground.com/ ('3 Season campground'; 'Open From May Long Weekend Until Thanksgiving'), read 2026-10-14; https://www.rothparkfamilycampground.com/uploads/1/0/7/2/107218429/2026_seasonal_rate_sheet.pdf ('OPEN: May Long Weekend'; 'CLOSED:Thanksgiving Weekend'), read 2026-10-14
note: Family campground just north of Wiarton, a few minutes' walk from Berford Lake, under new owners, the Pletch family.  A shallow sandy beach with a boat launch, canoe, kayak and paddle-boat rentals, and horseshoes, karaoke, potlucks and fireworks.  Seasonal sites have a waiting list going into 2026. --Claude

name: Harrison Park Campground
note: City of Owen Sound campground in historic Harrison Park; 100 full-service sites, some bordering the Sydenham River or Weavers' Creek, heated outdoor pool, restaurant, two playgrounds, direct Bruce Trail access. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct; reservable online. --Claude

name: Duins Pineridge Resort
note: Private resort on Pickerel Lake; limited overnight transient sites for travel trailers/RVs (no tents), 30-amp + water, including one lakefront site for smaller trailers; also seasonal sites and cottage rentals. Open ~May 15-Oct 15; beach, boat launch. Book early by phone. --Claude

name: Upper Canada Campground
note: Private family campground (the Wells family) at 13390 County Road 41, Morrisburg, three minutes from Upper Canada Village: 250 sites with fire pit and picnic table, 15/30/50-amp and water hookups, pull-throughs, RVs to 60 ft; two pools, a beach on a man-made pond, camp store, rec hall, laundry, dump station. 2026 rates for two people before HST: 15-amp C$48, 30-amp C$55, 50-amp C$65 a night. Open ~May-Sept, reservable online through Campspot. Corrected 2026-10-12: privately run, not a St. Lawrence Parks Commission campground as this note said. --Claude  SEASONAL SHARE: about 40 of its 250 sites take overnight campers and the rest are seasonal (ontariocamping.ca listing; Campspot books 41 RV sites), so book ahead (2026-10-12). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on July and August weekends, 3 on holiday weekends (uppercanadacampground.com rates page, 2026-10-12). --Claude

name: Riverland Lodge & Camp
note: Private four-season lodge & campground on the Madawaska River off Hwy 60, 15 min from Algonquin's East Gate; ~160 sites (156 RV/camper, 4 mobile-home), 30-amp water/electric with 50-amp serviced sites and 15 pull-throughs; playground, rec field, river beaches. Open ~May 15-Oct 15; reserve by phone. --Claude

name: Cedardale Camping & Seasonal Resort
note: Large lakeside resort on Lake Ontario near Carrying Place/Quinte West; ~200 sites — 179 seasonal + 28 overnight/transient + cottages. Full hookups, dump station, heated pool, private sandy beach, camp store, laundry; open May-Oct. Reservable online. Mostly-seasonal community but takes nightly overnighters. --Claude

name: Sutton Bay Park
note: Big-rig-friendly park on Lake Temiskaming (Sutton Bay) near New Liskeard/Temiskaming Shores; 100 overnight sites — 30 full-hookup (water/elec/sewer), 25 water/elec, pull-through — plus beach, pool, store; open ~late Apr-mid Oct. Reservable via operator. --Claude

name: Morning Mist Resort
note: Seasonal RV resort (early May-late Oct) on the Ottawa River just N of Algonquin Park, near Stonecliffe. ~54 sites: 40 full-hookup + 11 elec/water (30/50-amp), 3 pull-throughs, 3 tent; showers, laundry, dump, playground, 1300 ft sandy waterfront. Cottages & boat rentals; takes overnight campers. Book by phone. --Claude

name: The Willows Campground and RV Park
note: Family-owned campground on Longbow Lake Rd, 14 km E of Kenora. 90 sites (15/30/50-amp + unserviced), pool, laundry, store, showers, dump; open mid-May-Thanksgiving weekend, takes overnighters. Reservable. --Claude

name: Fort William Historical Park RV Park
note: Campground at the Ontario government living-history park on the Kaministiquia River, Thunder Bay. ~64 sites, ~17 with 50/30/20amp + water and the rest non-serviced (dry); dump station, showers; open Victoria Day through Thanksgiving weekend. Reservable. --Claude

name: Roberts Creek Provincial Park
note: Rustic BC Parks car campground inland in cedar/fir forest, ~2 km past Flume Rd off Hwy 101 between Gibsons and Sechelt. 21 vehicle-accessible sites (incl a double), all fitting RVs/trailers; open mid-May to early Sept. First-come, first-served; cash only. The Roberts Creek pier/beach day-use is a separate area. --Claude

name: Skagit Valley Provincial Park - Ross Lake Campground
note: Drive-in vehicle-accessible campground in Skagit Valley Provincial Park (BC Parks), on a bench above the braided Skagit River just north of the Ross Lake reservoir. Roughly 80+ gravel/grass sites, pit toilets, no hookups; group site by reservation. Access road open ~mid-April to mid-October. Mix of reservable and first-come sites. --Claude

name: Skagit Valley Provincial Park - Silvertip Campground
note: Drive-in vehicle-accessible campground in Skagit Valley Provincial Park (BC Parks) along the Silver-Skagit Road, 43 tent+RV sites, pit toilets, no hookups, open ~May 1 to early October. First-come, first-served (no online or phone reservations). --Claude

name: Sasquatch Provincial Park - Lakeside (Deer Lake) Campground
note: Drive-in campground in Sasquatch Provincial Park (BC Parks) on the west shore of Deer Lake, 42 vehicle-accessible sites taking RVs to ~32 ft; unserviced (no hookups) with a dump station in the park; open ~March to October. Reservable online (most sites). --Claude

name: Sasquatch Provincial Park - Bench Campground
note: Drive-in campground in Sasquatch Provincial Park (BC Parks), 64 vehicle-accessible sites taking RVs to ~32 ft; unserviced (no hookups), dump station in park, water taps throughout; open ~April to October. Reservable online (most sites). --Claude

name: Inkaneep Provincial Park
note: BC Parks; 7 small vehicle-accessible sites on the east bank of the Okanagan River, 6 km N of Oliver on Hwy 97. Pit toilets, no hookups, RV length limit ~25 ft (best for tents/small RVs). First-come, first-served (self-registration vault, cash); open ~mid-May to late Sept. --Claude

name: Jewel Lake Provincial Park
note: BC Parks; 26 vehicle-accessible sites at the north end of Jewel Lake, 12 km E of Greenwood off Hwy 3. Pit toilets, hand-pump water, no hookups. First-come, first-served (self-registration vault, cash); open ~mid-May to late Sept. --Claude

name: Nancy Greene Provincial Park
note: BC Parks campground at sub-alpine Nancy Greene Lake by the Hwy 3/3B junction: 10 parking-lot-style drive-in sites (suited to small RVs as a stopover) plus 1 walk-in tent site; cash self-registration, First-come, first-served (no reservations); open ~mid-May to Sept 30. --Claude

name: Cumberland Lake Park Campground
note: Municipal campground on Comox Lake operated by the Lake Park Society for the Village of Cumberland; 59 sites (20 serviced w/ power+water, 6 RV unserviced, 33 unserviced) plus 2 group sites; forested and lakefront site choices; boat launch and swimming beach. Open May-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Kitty Coleman Beach Provincial Park
note: Class C provincial park run by a community park board, 6 km NW of Courtenay. 65 vehicle-accessible drive-in oceanfront sites on the Strait of Georgia with pit toilets and running water, no hookups; open ~mid-Apr to Sep. First-come, first-served (not on the BC Parks reservation system) — call the caretaker. --Claude

name: Okanagan Lake Provincial Park - South Campground
note: South campground of Okanagan Lake Provincial Park, 11 km N of Summerland on the lake's W shore; ~88 drive-in sites (plus 8 walk-in tent), showers and flush toilets, water hookups, playground, boat launch; open ~late May to Sep. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Whiteswan Lake Provincial Park - Inlet Creek Campground
note: Whiteswan Lake Provincial Park's Inlet Creek campground (km 28), 16 vehicle-accessible sites on the east side of the road across from Whiteswan Lake, no hookups. First-come, first-served; self-register. Gravel FSR access, open May-Sept. --Claude

name: Adams Lake Provincial Park - Bush Creek Site
note: BC Parks rustic campground on the SW shore of Adams Lake, 15 km up a gravel road from Squilax (Hwy 1); 27 vehicle-accessible sites plus 4 walk-in, fire rings only, no potable water, no hookups, no pull-throughs, suited to campers and small trailers. Sandy beach and gravel boat launch. First-come, first-served, roughly May 15-Sep 30. --Claude

name: Tweedsmuir (South) Provincial Park - Fisheries Pool Campground
note: BC Parks vehicle-accessible campground in Tweedsmuir (South) on the Atnarko River along Hwy 20, up the valley from Stuie. 12 sites (open ~Jun 15-Oct 15), pit toilets, no hookups; most trailers/RVs fit. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Nisga'a Memorial Lava Bed Park - Vetter Creek Campground
note: Vetter Creek Campground in Nisga'a Memorial Lava Bed Park, beside the visitor centre near the T-junction on Hwy 113. 16 vehicle-accessible sites (large, double, and wheelchair-accessible), no hookups, water pump, pit/flush toilets, no showers, no sani-dump; sites shaded by deciduous forest. Self-register on site; first-come, first-served. Open May-Sept. --Claude

name: Red Bluff Provincial Park
note: Red Bluff Provincial Park campground on Babine Lake near Granisle. 27 vehicle-accessible tent/RV sites, no hookups, boat launch, swimming, fishing; known for iron-stained cliffs. Reservable online. Open mid-May to mid-Sept. --Claude

name: Buckinghorse River Wayside Provincial Park
note: BC Parks wayside on the Alaska Hwy (Hwy 97, ~km 278, ~200 km NW of Fort St John). 17 vehicle-accessible sites for RVs and tents, FCFS, $20/party/night; pit toilets, picnic tables, fire pits. Open ~May-Sept. Non-potable water (boil). First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Charlie Lake Provincial Park
note: BC Parks, 11 km N of Fort St John at the Alaska Hwy/Hwy 29 junction. 57 sites (elevated gravel pads, picnic table, fire ring; no hookups) — 40 reservable + 17 FCFS; cold water taps, pit toilets, sani-dump (fee), boat launch, playground, disc golf. Open ~May-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Moberly Lake Provincial Park
note: BC Parks, 25 km NW of Chetwynd off Hwy 29. 109 sites for RVs and tents (no hookups; RV length limit ~32 ft / 10 m) — 67 reservable + 42 FCFS; pit toilets, water taps, dump station, boat launch, playground. Open ~May-Sept. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Pine Le Moray Provincial Park, Heart Lake Campground
note: BC Parks, Hwy 97 ~71 km SW of Chetwynd. Heart Lake Campground has 13 FCFS sites (one double) suitable for tents and RVs of all sizes with some maneuvering (no pull-throughs, no hookups, no dump); 2 vault toilets, 2 water pumps (no drinking water), picnic tables, fire rings. Free. Electric-motor-free lake. Open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: SMONEĆTEN (McDonald) Campground
note: Gulf Islands NP frontcountry campground on the Saanich Peninsula near Sidney/Swartz Bay ferry; 49 primitive sites (43 drive-in + 6 bike/walk-in), no hookups, potable water + pit toilets; open mid-May-Sep 30. RV/motorhome accessible, no services. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Prior Centennial Campground
note: Gulf Islands NP frontcountry campground set in forest on North Pender Island (off Canal Rd); 17 primitive road-accessible (drive-in) sites, no hookups, potable water + pit toilets; open mid-May-Sep 30. Former BC Parks vehicle campground. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Green Point Campground
note: Pacific Rim NP Reserve campground above Long Beach between Ucluelet and Tofino; 94 vehicle drive-in sites all with 15/30A electrical (plus 20 walk-in), RV accessible; flush toilets, no showers; open ~May-mid-Oct and typically full all season. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Illecillewaet Campground
note: Glacier NP at Rogers Pass; 60 unserviced sites (no hookups), flush toilets, potable water, kitchen shelters, food lockers, staffed welcome station. ~Half the sites reservable, half first-come, first-served. Sites for large RVs are limited but small RVs/vans fit; basecamp for nine Rogers Pass trailheads. Open ~mid-June to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Loop Brook Campground
note: Glacier NP, ~5 km west of Rogers Pass summit; 20 level unserviced sites (no hookups), flush toilets, food lockers, log kitchen shelter, no potable water. Reservation-only. Suited to tents and small RVs/tent-trailers, with a few sites that take Class C motorhomes; open ~late June to mid-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Hoodoo Creek Campground
note: Yoho NP, ~24 km west of Field off the Trans-Canada; 30 unserviced sites (no hookups) on a sunny open meadow below Mt. Hunter, dry/outhouse toilets, kitchen shelter, firewood provided, no potable water. First-come, first-served. Parks Canada lists it for motorhomes and trailers up to 50 ft; near the Wapta Falls and Hoodoos trails. Open ~mid-June to early Sept. --Claude

name: Islandview Beach Regional Park
note: CRD regional park campground on the Salish Sea shore of the Saanich Peninsula; 18 beachfront RV sites plus treed tent-trailer/tent sites, self-contained (no hydro/dump/showers). Summer season (Victoria Day-Thanksgiving), all sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Horne Lake Regional Park, Paradise Bay Campground
note: RDN (Regional District of Nanaimo) regional park campground on Horne Lake, operated by RLC Parks concessionaire; ~51 non-serviced drive-in sites (most on the lake with paths to the beach), general store and boat launch, gravel access road. Reservable online (Apr-Oct). --Claude

name: Derby Reach Regional Park - Edgewater Bar Campground
note: Metro Vancouver regional park campground on the Fraser River at Edgewater Bar; 38 unserviced drive-in pads for tents/RVs, vault toilets, water spigots, no hookups/dump. Open Mar-Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Grand Forks Municipal Campground & City Park
note: City of Grand Forks municipal campground in City Park on the Kettle River; full-hookup (30/50-amp) and pull-through sites accommodating RVs to 40 ft, tent sites, showers, free sani-dump, sandy river beach. Open May-mid-Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Mount Baker RV Park
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: City of Cranbrook RV campground a short walk from downtown, run under contract for the city, with Joseph Creek running through it, power at most sites and washrooms; it is open from April to about Thanksgiving, and back-to-back bookings aren't allowed. --Claude

name: City of Trail RV Park
note: City of Trail municipal RV park at the east entrance to the city off Highway 3B by Waneta Plaza; 31 sites (serviced, partial-service and gravel/grassed), flush toilets, hot showers, wifi, playground, sani-station and firewood. Open May to Labour Day. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Beaver Valley Family Park
note: Regional District of Kootenay Boundary / Beaver Valley Recreation campground about 3-5 km east of Fruitvale off Highway 3B; tent and RV sites with 30-amp electrical, water and some pull-throughs, plus toilets, hot showers, kitchen shelter, disc golf, pickleball and playground; fishing in nearby Marsh Creek. Open May long weekend to Labour Day. Reservable via the Beaver Valley Recreation office. --Claude

name: Broughton Strait Campsite
note: Town of Port McNeill campground on SE Main Rd, in coastal forest a short walk from town and the ferry terminal. Fully serviced RV sites plus tent sites (power/water), free hot showers, laundry, fire pits + picnic tables. Small (~10-20 sites); daily/weekly/monthly rates. Reserve by phone/email. Open roughly May-Sep. --Claude

name: Golden Municipal Campground and RV Park
note: Town of Golden municipal campground on the Kicking Horse River in downtown Golden; ~72-77 sites with 30-amp electric (some electric+water), pull-throughs, showers, laundry, dump station, onsite store; open ~Apr-Oct. Run by a concessionaire. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Quesnel Downtown RV Park & Campground
note: City of Quesnel downtown municipal campground on the Quesnel River, within walking distance of downtown via the Riverfront Trail; 14 serviced RV sites (30-amp + water), 3 unserviced RV, 3 tent; city sani-dump nearby. Open ~May-Sep. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Riverside Municipal RV Park & Campground
note: Town of Smithers municipal campground on the Bulkley River; 43 sites with 15/30-amp electric, water and sewer hookups, flush toilets/showers, playground, camp kitchen, nature/bike trails; open ~May 15-Oct 1, 14-day max stay. Reservable online plus FCFS within 3 days of arrival. --Claude

name: Riverside Park Campground
note: District of Vanderhoof park campground on the wooded bank of the Nechako River, 10-min walk to downtown; 38 sites incl 2 pull-through and 3 doubles, water + electric (5 sites 50A), showers. Reservable online (May-Oct). --Claude

name: Monkman RV Park
note: Full-service RV park in the heart of Tumbler Ridge; 54 pull-through sites with 30A power, water and sewer, plus tent/overflow area, showers and laundry, sani-dump. Open May-Sep, reservable. --Claude

name: Lions Flatbed Creek Campground
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: District of Tumbler Ridge campground in a creek setting on Flatbed Creek, 1 km from town, with fire pits, firewood, a cooking shelter, picnic areas, a playground, hiking trails and a swimming hole.  The district says it is open from May to September; the tourism site says May to October. --Claude

name: Rainey Creek Municipal Campground
note: District of Stewart municipal campground on Rainey Creek within walking distance of downtown Stewart (gateway to Hyder AK); RV sites with 30A/15A electrical plus dry sites and tent sites, modern shower house, covered picnic/cooking areas. Open mid-May to mid-Sep, reservable. --Claude

name: Tetsa River Regional Park
note: Northern Rockies Regional Municipality park on the Alaska Highway (~96 km NW of Fort Nelson) beside the Tetsa River; 25 unserviced forested sites (sites 1-13 fit large motorhomes, 17-25 up to 27 ft), hand-pump non-potable water, picnic shelter, playground. $20/night, reservable online plus drop-in. Open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Mowhinna Creek Campground
note: Private campground ~1 km south of Ganges on Salt Spring Island; serviced RV sites with power/water/septic ('easily accessible for large units'), plus power-only and tent sites and 2 small sleeping cabins. Reservable online; open seasonally. --Claude

name: Fairy Lake Recreation Site
note: RSTBC Crown recreation site (managed by Silvifor) 5 km NE of Port Renfrew on Fairy Lake, via gravel Harris Main; 36 sites (16 reservable via VICamping, 16 FCFS), some large enough for RVs, sandy beach; rustic - pit toilets, no potable water, pack-in/out. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Maple Grove Recreation Site
note: RSTBC Crown recreation site (managed by Silvifor) on the north shore of Cowichan Lake near Youbou; ~82 lakeside sites (reservable + FCFS via VICamping, cash for FCFS), RV-accessible, pit toilets, boat launch, south-facing beach. Open ~May-Oct. --Claude

name: Caycuse Campground
note: Campground on Mosaic Forest Management private timberland (managed by Silvifor) on the south shore of Cowichan Lake; permits tents, motorhomes, trailers and fifth wheels; reached via ~11 km gravel forest road (all vehicles); reservable online through Mosaic Campsites. Open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Brannen Lake RV Park & Campsite
note: Family-owned 49-acre park on Brannen Lake, 120+ drive-in sites from full-hookup (30A power/water/sewer) to unserviced tenting; pull-thrus, big-rig friendly, boat launch and private sandy beach. Open May-mid-Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Whistle Stop RV & Tent Park
note: Seasonal (May-Nov) RV/tent park off Hwy 1 at St Elmo Rd near Hope; 39 sites (6 full-hookup, 18 elec/water, 15 tent), free showers, laundry, sani-dump, playground, store; reservable. Named for adjacent rail line (some train/highway noise). --Claude

name: River's Edge RV Park
note: Small family RV & tent park on the Similkameen River behind Kal Tire off Hwy 3, a 10-min walk from Princeton; large partly-serviced grassy sites, restrooms, WiFi, dump station, fire pits, eagle-viewing deck. Open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Springbrook Resort
note: Private motel + RV park at 4527 Hwy 93/95, Skookumchuck, beside the Kootenay River. 52 total sites incl 16 full-hookup (30-amp) and 2 pull-through RV sites plus 4 tent sites; showers, coin laundry, store, cold pond beach, river walking path. Open May-Oct; reservable by phone/email. --Claude

name: Pierre's Point Campground
note: Family campground on Shuswap Lake at Tappen Bay (2569 Campground Rd), managed by the Adams Lake Indian Band. Treed drive-in sites: full-hookup pull-throughs (30-amp) + partial-hookup + tenting, dump station, laundry, showers, sandy beach, playground, mini-golf. Open ~mid-Apr to mid-Sep; reservable online. --Claude

name: Shuswap Falls RV Resort
note: 37-acre riverfront resort on the Shuswap River near Mabel Lake, 2202 Enderby-Mabel Lake Rd, ~22 km E of Enderby. 132 treed full-service sites (30-amp/water/sewer) with ~1200 ft of riverfront; pool, boat launch, playground. Many sites are member-owned but limited nightly/overnight transient sites are available (confirmed by 2026 reviews, rigs to 50+ ft). Open ~mid-Apr to Thanksgiving. --Claude

name: Lumby Lions Campground
note: Lions service-club campground 3 blocks from downtown Lumby at 2215 Shields Ave, on Duteau Creek. 16 drive-in sites with 30-amp power + water, plus tent sites; showers/washrooms, fire rings; ball park/pool/tennis nearby. Open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Knouff Lake Wilderness Resort
season_source: note prose (cleaned out of the note 2026-10-13)
note: Resort on Knouff Lake, established in 1904 and one of the oldest in B.C., 45 minutes from Kamloops and 30 from Sun Peaks; it holds a North American fly-fishing record for a 17.5 lb dry-fly catch.  RV sites have power and water or no hookups at all, and there is a walk-in tent island, the Hideaway group site for up to five trailers, year-round rustic cabins fitted with cast-iron wood cook stoves, rental trailers, boat rentals and a family beach.  Wi-Fi reaches only the lodge; generators may run from 8 to 10 a.m. and 5 to 7 p.m., and the gate is closed overnight (10 p.m. to 8 a.m. in summer, 9 p.m. to 9 a.m. in winter). --Claude

name: Kokanee Bay Resort
note: Private lakeside resort on Lac La Hache off Hwy 97 (3728 Hwy 97); ~50 sites incl 15/30-amp full-service and pull-thru sites for larger units, plus motel/cabins, sandy beach, boat docks, showers, laundry, store. Open ~May-Oct. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Cariboo Bonanza Resort
note: Private resort on Horse Lake near Lone Butte (6384 Watson Rd); 56 sites incl 18 pull-through and 50 full-hookup RV sites (plus 6 tent), each with firepit/picnic table, showers, laundry, dump station, boat access. Open ~May-Sep. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Little Horse Lodge
note: Cariboo lodge on Hwy 97 at 70 Mile House, a short walk across the road from Green Lake. ~16-19 gravel drive-in RV sites at the back of the property with 30-amp power and water, spacious for big rigs; also cabins, restaurant, general store and horse paddocks; open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Dutch Lake Resort & RV Park
note: Lakeside resort/motel on Dutch Lake, ~1 km off Hwy 5 in Clearwater (gateway to Wells Gray). ~65 fully serviced RV sites with 30/50-amp power, water and sewer, incl. 2 premium lakeside sites; big rigs OK, picnic table+fire pit per site, showers, laundry, on-site restaurant; open ~Apr-Oct. Reservable. --Claude

name: Williams Lake Stampede Campground
note: Non-profit campground run by the Williams Lake Stampede Association (community volunteer society) at the stampede grounds off Hwy 97/Mackenzie Ave. 58 full-service RV sites (1-49 30-amp, 50-58 50-amp) with water/sewer, plus tent sites and a dump station; laundry, showers. Open mid-April to mid-October, reservable. Horse/livestock trailers not permitted in the campground. --Claude

name: Cariboo Joy RV Park
note: Hosted full-service private RV park in the gold-rush town of Wells, ~5 min before Barkerville on Barkerville Hwy (Hwy 26). 30 gravel sites (pull-thru and back-in) with 30/20-amp power, water, sewer, central sani-station; flush toilets, hot showers, firepits, game room. Walkable to town amenities. Open mid-May to late Sept. --Claude

name: iRVin's RV Park and Campground
note: Private RV park at 360 Loseth Rd on the Yellowhead Hwy just north of Valemount, open Apr-Oct. ~96 sites: full-service pull-thrus with 30/50-amp power/water/sewer plus grassed water-only tent sites; coin laundry, free showers/WiFi, camp store, propane. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Yellowhead Campground and RV Park
note: Private campground on 30 acres at 325 North Hwy 5, edge of Valemount, bordering Swift Creek; open Apr-Sep. 44 powered RV sites (power/water/table/fire pit) plus 28 tent + 3 group tent sites; washrooms, free hot showers, sani-dump, laundry; walk to town. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Kitwanga River RV Campground
note: Private RV park on the Kitwanga River just off the Cassiar Hwy (Hwy 37), open May-Oct. ~55 sites incl 21 pull-thrus and 25 full-hookup (20/30-amp); big-rig friendly with dump station, showers, laundry. Class-2 river fishing (steelhead/salmon) on-site. Reserve by phone. --Claude

name: Ferry Island Campground
note: City of Terrace municipal campground on Ferry Island in the Skeena River, 3.5 km from downtown, open May-Sep. 103 sites incl tent, RV and fully-serviced (water hookups) with pull-thrus for big rigs; hot showers, firewood, trails and tree carvings in the surrounding 150-acre park. --Claude

name: Northern Experience RV Park
note: Private big-rig-friendly RV park at 9180 Hwy 97 S, ~6 min south of Prince George. 55 sites with pull-thrus, full and partial hookups, laundry, showers, 5-acre dog walk, playground; open ~Mar-Nov. --Claude

name: MamaYeh RV Park & Campground
note: Private RV park at 5235 White Rd off Hwy 97 S, ~15 min south of Prince George, set in a forested 145-acre parcel. 36 sites incl 100-ft pull-thrus with 50-amp power and full hookups plus unserviced sites; big-rig friendly, wide green buffers between sites; open ~May-Sep. --Claude

name: Bee Lazee RV Park & Campground
note: Private RV park & campground at 15910 Hwy 97 S, south of Prince George. 49 sites - 21 pull-thrus, 28 full hookups, 3 electric/water, plus tent sites; heated pool, showers, laundry, playground, Wi-Fi; open ~May-mid Sep. --Claude

name: Hartway RV Park
note: Private RV park (also B&B) in a wooded residential area on the Hart Highway (Hwy 97) north side of Prince George; 40 sites incl 3 pull-throughs and 35 full-hookup (30/50-amp) plus a grass tent/overflow area. Laundry, showers, WiFi, sani-dump/water fill. Open ~Apr-Oct, reservable by phone/online. --Claude

name: West Lake Campground and RV Park
note: Family-owned private campground on 26 wooded acres off Blackwater Rd ~12 km west of Prince George, ~1 mi from West Lake Provincial Day Park; ~35 sites with full/partial hookups plus non-serviced 'Mega' sites (and 3 cabins). Laundry, hot showers, flush toilets, WiFi. Open ~May-mid Sept, reservable online/phone. --Claude

name: Stone Creek RV Park
note: Small private riverside campground at 31605 Hwy 97S, ~35 km south of Prince George on the Fraser River; ~12 power sites plus many tent/non-power sites, potable water, showers, walking trails with creek/river access and sites along the Fraser. Seasonal May-mid Oct. Camper-reported rate: C$30-45 a night (Campendium, June and August 2025). --Claude

name: Brown Bird RV Park
note: Private RV park on Hwy 37 in Dease Lake (Stewart-Cassiar); formerly Dease Lake RV Park, under newer management. ~34 sites incl 6 pull-throughs, full hookups, big-rig friendly, laundry/showers/dump. Open May-Sep. Camper-reported rate: C$54-60 a night (Campendium, August and October 2025). --Claude

name: Toad River Lodge & RV Park
note: Historic Alaska Highway lodge (Mile 422) on Reflection Lake, Toad River. 23-site full-service RV park, pull-through & back-in, full hookups + fire rings, wifi, laundry; gas/diesel, cafe on site. Full service early May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Peace Island Park
note: Municipal campground on an island in the Peace River at Taylor; BC Hydro land leased and operated by the District of Taylor via a contractor. ~81 serviced sites (57 in the expansion area + 24 full-service) plus ~40 non-powered sites; boat launch, playground, trails, cookhouse. Seasonal (opens May). Reservable online. --Claude

name: Snaring Campground
note: Jasper NP FCFS unserviced campground, 62 sites north of the townsite off Snaring Rd near the Snaring/Athabasca River; fire pits, no hookups or showers; Parks Canada lists sites for rigs under 27 ft (fits 23-ft EKKO). First-come, first-served (mid-May to late Sept). Unaffected by the 2024 Jasper wildfire. --Claude

name: Honeymoon Lake Campground
note: Jasper NP FCFS unserviced campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93) at Honeymoon Lake, 34 sites; primitive (no hookups), rigs under 27 ft per Parks Canada. First-come, first-served (late May to mid-Sept). --Claude

name: Mount Kerkeslin Campground
note: Jasper NP FCFS unserviced campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93) ~36 km south of the townsite along the Athabasca River; 42 sites, primitive (fire rings, outhouses, no hookups), rigs under 27 ft per Parks Canada; sandy river bank with natural canoe launch. First-come, first-served (mid-May to mid-Sept). --Claude

name: Tunnel Mountain Trailer Court
note: Banff NP campground on the Tunnel Mountain bench, 322 sites with full three-way hookups (water/sewer/electric 15/30/50A), rigs to 15 m (50 ft); reservable, open ~early May to early Oct. Short walk to Banff townsite. --Claude

name: Tunnel Mountain Village I Campground
note: Banff NP campground on the Tunnel Mountain bench, 618 unserviced sites (many with fire pits), rigs to ~8 m (27 ft); reservable, open ~mid-May to early Oct. Banff's largest campground; short walk to townsite. --Claude

name: Icefields Centre RV (Columbia Icefield)
note: Jasper NP FCFS overnight RV area at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93); ~100 primitive drive-in sites for self-contained RVs/trailers only, no water and no fires, elev ~1960 m. First-come, first-served (mid-May to mid-Oct). Separate from the adjacent tent-only Icefield walk-in campground. --Claude

name: Silverhorn Creek Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93), ~46 km N of Lake Louise. 45 unserviced reservable sites (no hookups; no water on site — potable water/sani-dump at Waterfowl Lakes), motorhomes/trailers to 20 m. Reservation only, season ~late May–late Sep. --Claude

name: Protection Mountain Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Bow Valley Parkway (Hwy 1A) between Castle Jct and Lake Louise. 72 unserviced sites, RVs/trailers to 10 m, reservation only, open ~mid-Jun–mid-Sep. --Claude

name: Johnston Canyon Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Bow Valley Parkway across from Johnston Canyon, ~25 km NW of Banff. 132 unserviced sites (flush toilets, showers), RVs/trailers to 8.2 m, reservable, open ~late May–late Sep. --Claude

name: Rampart Creek Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway (Hwy 93) ~12 km N of Saskatchewan River Crossing, near the North Saskatchewan River. 51 unserviced sites, RVs/trailers to 10 m, reservation only, open ~late May–mid-Sep. --Claude

name: Two Jack Lakeside Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the shore of Two Jack Lake near Lake Minnewanka, ~13 km NE of Banff. 74 unserviced sites (includes some walk-in tent sites), RVs/trailers to 8.2 m, reservable, open ~late May–early Oct. --Claude

name: Waterfowl Lakes Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway between Upper and Lower Waterfowl Lakes (Mistaya River), ~57 km N of Lake Louise. 110 unserviced sites, RVs/trailers to 9 m, sani-dump on site, first-come first-served only (non-reservable), open ~mid-Jun–early Sep. --Claude

name: Mosquito Creek Campground
note: Parks Canada campground on the Icefields Parkway ~24 km N of Lake Louise, at Mosquito Creek. 38 unserviced sites, RVs/trailers to 10 m, first-come first-served only (non-reservable), open ~mid-Jun–mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Astotin Lake Campground
note: Elk Island NP; 75 unserviced sites including a 23-site RV loop (some pull-through) plus a walk-in tent area, RVs best under ~8m; showers, dump station, potable water, no hookups; reservable ~mid-May-Thanksgiving. --Claude

name: Peter Lougheed Provincial Park - Interlakes Campground
note: 48 unserviced (no hookups) sites on a wooded point on the east shore of Lower Kananaskis Lake in Peter Lougheed PP; about 23 sites back onto the lake. Mix of reservable and first-come sites (2026); max RV roughly 27 ft. Boat launch and sewage disposal nearby. Open mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Spray Valley Provincial Park - Spray Lakes West Campground
note: Unserviced FCFS sites (about 50-63) along the Spray Lake reservoir in Spray Valley PP, 16 km south of Canmore via the gravel Smith-Dorrien/Spray Trail (Hwy 742); vault toilets, hand-pump (non-potable) water. First-come, first-served; larger rigs can navigate the maintained gravel access. Open roughly mid-May to mid-Sep. --Claude

name: Chain Lakes Provincial Park
note: 88 reservable sites (31 unserviced, 57 with 15/30-amp power) in fan-shaped loops on Chain Lakes Reservoir, 38 km SW of Nanton on Hwy 533; RVs/trailers to 40 ft. Boat launch, sewage disposal, cooking shelter. Reservable online, 90 days out. Open early May to late Sep. --Claude

name: Gooseberry Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks campground in Gooseberry PRA, 10 km W of Bragg Creek on Hwy 66 in aspen/pine forest near the Elbow River. 85 sites (51 with power, 28 unserviced, 6 walk-in); reservable via Alberta Parks, open ~mid-May to early Oct. --Claude

name: Lundbreck Falls Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA 25 km NW of Pincher Creek off Hwy 3 along the Crowsnest River, below Lundbreck Falls. 46 RV sites (29 powered, 17 unserviced) in two loops plus 12 walk-in tent sites; some pull-throughs. No potable water - bring your own. Reservable via Alberta Parks, open ~mid-May to Sep. --Claude

name: Oldman Dam PRA - Cottonwood Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground in Oldman Dam PRA, 13 km N of Pincher Creek on Hwy 785 by the Oldman River/Reservoir. 82 shady sites (30 with 30A power, 52 unserviced) suited to RVs and tents, open ~May-Oct. Reservable via Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Oldman Dam PRA - Castleview Campground
note: Alberta Parks fully-serviced campground in Oldman Dam PRA, 13 km N of Pincher Creek on Hwy 785 by the Oldman River/Reservoir. 29 sites with power/water/sewer (15/30A) and privacy partitions, showers and dump station, RVs to ~50 ft. Reservable via Alberta Parks, open ~May-Sep. --Claude

name: Island Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: 40 unserviced sites in a rustic mountain-valley campground on Island Lake, 14 km W of Coleman in Crowsnest Pass; sites accommodate RVs. First-come, first-served (self-registration, cash/cheque). No potable water. Open May-Oct. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Oldman River Provincial Recreation Area
note: 25 unserviced sites (some reservable, some FCFS; includes pull-throughs) along the Oldman River under mature cottonwoods, ~5 km SW of Fort Macleod. Vault toilets, non-potable water. Open mid-May-Sep. Reservable online. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Beaver Mines Lake Campground (Castle Provincial Park)
note: 79 unserviced reservable sites for RVs and tents in Castle Provincial Park on Beaver Mines Lake, ~20 km W of Pincher Creek; boat launch, pit/vault toilets, non-potable water pump. Most sites treed, some with lake views. Reservable online. Open mid-May-late Sep. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: St. Mary Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area - St. Mary Lower Campground
note: 36 sites (35 powered 15/30A + 1 unserviced), all reservable, at the base of the St. Mary dam within a river oxbow ~5 km NW of Magrath; mature trees, playground, some sites back onto the water. Non-potable water. Open mid-May-Oct. Reservable online. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Police Outpost Provincial Park
note: 45 unserviced sites, all reservable, set in a poplar forest near Outpost Lake in Police Outpost Provincial Park, ~25 km SW of Cardston; boat launch, fescue-grassland/aspen interpretive trails. Bring water (non-potable). Open ~Apr-Oct. Reservable online. Per Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Waterton Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA on Waterton Reservoir, 25 km S then E of Pincher Creek. 25 unserviced tent/RV sites, first-come first-served per Alberta Parks; boat launch, pier, firepits, pit toilets, hand pump (non-potable). Open May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Castle River Bridge Campground (Castle PP)
note: Alberta Parks campground in Castle Provincial Park on the Castle River, ~20 km W of Pincher Creek on Hwy 507 then S on Hwy 774. ~25-30 powered (30-amp) drive-in sites for RVs and tents, wooded, pit/vault toilets, standpipe water; reservable via shop.albertaparks.ca (90-day window). Open ~mid-May to Sept. Separate comfort-camping cabins exist but the campground itself is real RV sites. --Claude

name: Greenford Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small Alberta Parks PRA campground on the Highwood River, ~22 km W of Longview on Hwy 541. 13 unserviced sites (no hookups) with firepits, picnic shelter, pit toilets and hand-pump water (fire use only; bring drinking water). First-come, first-served; open ~mid-May to early Sept. Fishing from camp. --Claude

name: Indian Graves Campground (Indian Graves PRA)
note: South Kananaskis PRA campground off the Cowboy Trail (29 km S of Longview on Hwy 22, 13 km W on Hwy 532), bordered by Johnson and Willow creeks; 38 unserviced sites for RVs and tents (lower loop ~21 sites with creek access) plus 6 equestrian sites. No hookups/power, outhouses, non-potable hand pump. Open mid-May to mid-Oct; some sites now reservable on shop.albertaparks.ca (contractor-managed by Wild Rose Campground Mgmt), rest FCFS. --Claude

name: Woolford Provincial Park
note: 17-20 unserviced drive-in sites on gravel pads suitable for RVs and trailers, on the St. Mary River ~50 km SW of Lethbridge (Hwy 5 then Hwy 503); pit toilets, water pumps, fire rings. Large open gravel sites with limited shade, a few more wooded. Reservable up to 90 days out. Open mid-May to late Sept. --Claude

name: Goldeye Lake Campground
note: Alberta Parks auto-access campground on Goldeye Lake, 8 km W of Nordegg off Hwy 11 then 3 km N on access road. 40+ unserviced sites in aspen/spruce; vault toilets, hand-pump (non-potable) water, boat launch, loop trail; stocked trout lake. Mix of reservable and first-come sites. Open ~May-Sept. --Claude

name: Crimson Lake Provincial Park - Twin Lakes Campground
note: Auto-access campground at Crimson Lake PP, ~15 km NW of Rocky Mountain House. 39 unserviced reservable sites in two loops (A treed, B open) at Twin Lakes; vault toilets, non-potable hand pump, playground; showers/laundry/dump station available at nearby main Crimson Lake campground. Suits small-medium RVs/trailers. Open ~May-mid-Oct. --Claude

name: Wolf Lake West Campground
note: Remote Alberta Parks auto-access campground on Wolf Lake, ~20 km E of Edson then ~53 km S on Wolf Lake Rd. 36 unserviced sites (some closed after past wildfire), first-come, first-served - no reservations. Boat launch, fish-cleaning stations, vault toilets, non-potable hand pump (bring drinking water). Open ~mid-May-late Sept. --Claude

name: Beaverdam Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small FCFS provincial forest campground on Shunda Creek ~5 km east of Nordegg off Hwy 11. 10 sites: 7 walk-in tent + 3 vehicle pull-up sites for smaller trailers/truck campers (open cleared loops on satellite fit a 23-ft rig), all unserviced; firepits, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Brazeau River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small treed FCFS provincial campground along the Brazeau River, 72 km north of Nordegg on Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734); managed by West Fraser Mills. 7 unserviced drive-in sites, cook shelter, firepits, free firewood, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Brown Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small treed FCFS provincial campground 45 km north of Nordegg on Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734); managed by West Fraser Mills. 7-8 unserviced drive-in sites, firepits, free firewood, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Burnt Timber Provincial Recreation Area
note: FCFS provincial campground on Burnt Timber Creek, ~70 km north of Hwy 1A on Hwy 40 near Water Valley. ~28-30 sites, vehicle-access drive-in on the north side of the creek plus some walk-in tent sites, all unserviced; firepits, picnic tables, pit toilets; bring own drinking water (hand-pump water not potable). Open ~May-Sep. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Chambers Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: FCFS provincial campground near Chambers Creek, west of Rocky Mountain House off Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734). About 25 unserviced drive-in sites, firepits, pit toilets; bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Dry Haven Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small FCFS provincial campground 11 km west of Nordegg on Hwy 11. 14 unserviced drive-in sites, cook shelter, firepits, pit toilets; no water pump on site, bring own drinking water. Open ~May-Oct. First-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Harlech Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA 13 km E of Nordegg on Hwy 11. 17 non-serviced, well-treed sites suitable for RVs and tents; firepits, pump water, outhouses. Fishing in Shunda Creek and a stocked trout pond; sites 12-17 are OHV rail-trail access sites. First-come, first-served (not reservable); open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Lovett River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA ~40 km S of Robb on Hwy 40; access road normally passable by 2WD. Quaint campground of 17 well-spaced treed sites; picnic tables, water, toilets. Trout/whitefish fishing and canoeing on the Lovett River, plus hiking trails. First-come, first-served; open May-Sep. --Claude

name: McLeod River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA 23 km SE of Hinton via the Robb Rd, along the McLeod River near the Gregg/McLeod confluence. Unserviced treed sites in a northern and southern loop; complimentary firewood, hand-pump water (non-potable, bring your own), pit toilets. Mix of reservable (online ABPP + phone) and first-come, first-served; open mid-May to end of October. --Claude

name: Mitchell Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small rustic Alberta Parks PRA 19 km S of Rocky Mountain House on Hwy 22, then 10 km W on a gravel access road. 5 sites: 3 open unserviced gravel drive-in sites next to the parking lot plus 2 walk-in tent sites; pit toilets, fishing piers and canoe/kayak hand-launch on Mitchell Lake. First-come, first-served; open mid-May to early Sept. Only the ~3 open gravel sites suit a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Pembina Forks Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA 63 km SE of Robb on Hwy 40, along the Pembina River. 20 large, well-spaced unserviced spruce-treed sites; firepits, complimentary firewood, vault toilets, hand-pump water. Reservable by phone with some first-come, first-served sites; open May to October. --Claude

name: Swan Lake Campground (Swan Lake Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA on Swan Lake, ~40 km SW of Rocky Mountain House. 24 unserviced drive-in sites (RVs and tents), most treed with a few next to the lake; boat launch, pier, fish-cleaning stations, pit toilets, hand-pump (non-potable) water, firewood for sale. First-come, first-served; ~$28/night; season mid-May to early Sept. Trophy trout/pike lake, electric motors/canoes only. OHVs must stay trailered until nearby trails. --Claude

name: Tay River Campground (Tay River Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA on the Tay River, 16 km SW of Caroline on Hwy 591. ~32 unserviced drive-in sites (RVs and tents), most in an open grassy field with a few along the riverbank; firepits, pit toilets, hand-pump (non-potable) water, firewood for sale. First-come, first-served; ~$28/night; season mid-May to early Sept. OHVs prohibited in the park; horses not permitted. --Claude

name: West Canal Campground (Brazeau Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA on Brazeau Reservoir, SW of Drayton Valley. West Canal is a small well-treed loop with ~18 gravel-pad drive-in sites near the water; hand-pump water, dry toilets, group shelter, firewood for sale. Reservable online; season May-Sept. Reservoir fishing, boating, canoeing; OHV trails nearby (prohibited in the campground). --Claude

name: Whitehorse Creek Campground (Whitehorse Creek Provincial Recreation Area)
note: Alberta Parks PRA and staging area for Whitehorse Wildland PP, ~6 km SW of Cadomin on a gravel access road, along Whitehorse Creek near its confluence with the McLeod River. 26 unserviced drive-in sites (17 general + 9 equestrian with corrals/pens/tie stalls); firepits, free firewood, pit toilets, hand-pump water. Reservations recommended (equestrian sites by phone; one FCFS site); operated by West Fraser Mills; season May-Oct. General campground that also offers horse sites. --Claude

name: Miquelon Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park ~68 km SE of Edmonton. Miquelon Lake campground has 269 sites (82 unserviced, 187 powered 15/30A) across A/B/C areas, showers, flush toilets, two dump stations. Reservable May-Oct via reservation.albertaparks.ca; a handful of Loop A sites are winter FCFS. Suited to tents and RVs. --Claude

name: Red Lodge Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park on the Little Red Deer River, 15 km W of Bowden on Hwy 587. 79 sites (42 unserviced, 37 powered 15/30A), most spacious enough for trailers/RVs. Reservable May-Sep. For 2026 the sani-dump/fill, showers and flush toilets are closed for wastewater repairs (vault toilets only; alt sani-dump in Bowden). --Claude

name: Jarvis Bay Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park 4 km N of Sylvan Lake off Hwy 20. Main campground ~193 sites, virtually all powered (15/30A), well-treed with drive-through sites accommodating large RVs; a separate North Loop is tent-only. Reservable May-Sep (sites 186-195 add FCFS after early Sep). Showers, flush toilets, RV fill station. --Claude

name: Medicine Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA, rustic lakeside camping ~47 km N of Rocky Mountain House then 12 km on gravel road. 48 unserviced sites (loops A/B/C), well-treed with some lakeside sites, dry toilets; bring your own water. RV and tent, mostly reservable May-Oct with 6 FCFS sites (A-10/A-11/B-23/B-24/C-44/C-45). --Claude

name: Pigeon Lake Provincial Park - Zeiner Campground
note: Zeiner campground in Alberta Parks' Pigeon Lake Provincial Park (Mulhurst side). 117 sites (26 unserviced, 83 powered 15/30A, 8 walk-in tent), pull-through options, showers, flush toilets, dump station. Reservation-only May-Sep (no FCFS). --Claude

name: Pigeon Lake Provincial Park - Pigeon Lake Campground
note: Main campground in Alberta Parks' Pigeon Lake Provincial Park (Westerose side). 247 sites (106 unserviced, 131 powered, 10 full-hookup power/water/sewer), suited to tents and RVs; boat launch, showers, flush toilets, playground. Reservable May-Sep with a minimum of 10 Loop A powered sites FCFS year-round. --Claude

name: Dickson Point Campground (Gleniffer Reservoir PRA)
note: Alberta Parks campground on a point in Gleniffer Reservoir (Dickson Dam), ~20 km west of Innisfail south of Hwy 54. 18 unserviced sites, large open sites well suited to RVs; vault toilets, boat launch, non-potable hand pump (bring drinking water/firewood). First-come, first-served; open ~mid-May to late Sept, ~$28. --Claude

name: Brewers Campground (Aspen Beach Provincial Park)
note: One of two campgrounds (Brewers + Lakeview, ~200 sites total) at Aspen Beach PP on the south shore of Gull Lake, ~18 km west of Lacombe on Hwy 12. Brewers sites are treed with water hookup + sewage disposal (no power); flush toilets, showers, boat launch, playground. Reservable online; open ~May-Oct. Note: Gull Lake boat launches closed due to critically low water levels. --Claude

name: Rochon Sands Provincial Park
note: Provincial park on the shore of Buffalo Lake, ~12 km west of Stettler off Hwy 12; operated by the Summer Village of Rochon Sands. ~67 RV sites plus walk-in tenting and group sites, in open lakeside spots and treed loops; pit toilets, tap water, dump station, boat launch, fish-cleaning station, playground. Reservable online (Campspot); open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude

name: North Dyke Campground (Gleniffer Reservoir PRA)
note: Alberta Parks campground on the north shore of Gleniffer Reservoir (Dickson Dam), ~20 km west of Innisfail south of Hwy 54. 30 unserviced sites; large, level sites ideal for RVs and tents; firepits, vault toilets, boat launch, non-potable hand pump (bring drinking water/firewood). First-come, first-served; open ~mid-May to late Sept. --Claude

name: Cartier Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks rec area on the upper Red Deer River, ~22 km southwest of Sundre on Coalcamp Road (gravel). 12 unserviced, well-spaced treed sites; vault toilets, firepits, bring your own water/firewood; river fishing and canoe/kayak access. First-come, first-served; open ~late Apr to mid-Sept. Operated by the non-profit FOESA under Alberta Parks. --Claude

name: Fallen Timber North Campground (Fallen Timber PRA)
note: Alberta Parks rec area in the foothills on Fallen Timber Creek, ~25 km southwest of Sundre off Hwy 22 via gravel roads. 34 unserviced, well-treed sites (some riverside); pit toilets, firepits, firewood included, non-potable hand pump. First-come, first-served; open ~May to mid-Oct. Narrow gravel campground roads — best suited to smaller/mid-size rigs; operated by Red Rock Sawmills. Keep OHVs trailered in the rec area. --Claude

name: Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park - Tolman East Campground
note: East-bank Red Deer River valley campground in Dry Island Buffalo Jump PP, near Tolman Bridge (~33 km south of the park day-use area). 40 unserviced sites tucked under cottonwoods, sheltered, suitable for tents and RVs; hand boat launch, playground, pit/vault toilets, water pump, no firewood. First-come, first-served; vehicle access closed mid-Oct to mid-May. --Claude

name: Dry Island Buffalo Jump Provincial Park - Tolman West Campground
note: West-bank campground in Dry Island Buffalo Jump PP at Tolman Bridge on the Red Deer River. 25 large open unserviced sites well suited to RVs; cooking shelter, fire pits, hand launch, pit/vault toilets, water pump, no firewood. First-come, first-served; vehicle access closed mid-Oct to mid-May. --Claude

name: Phyllis Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Foothills lake recreation area 16 km west of Caroline (Hwy 22 then Hwy 591). 21 unserviced sites, most open and facing Phyllis Lake; hand pump (non-potable), outhouses, fire pits, fish-cleaning station. First-come, first-served; open mid-May to late Sept; electric-motor boating only. --Claude

name: The Narrows Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small secluded recreation area on the channel connecting the two basins of Buffalo Lake, ~40 km west of Stettler; operated by the Summer Village of Rochon Sands under lease from Alberta Parks (land remains provincial). Treed RV/tent sites along the narrows; first-come, first-served, cash/cheque only. Bring water; access closed mid-Oct to early May. --Claude

name: Vermilion Provincial Park
note: Provincial park on a Vermilion River reservoir adjacent to the Town of Vermilion (town operates the campground under Alberta Parks). 118 RV-suitable sites: 18 full-hookup, 4 power/water, 68 power, 28 unserviced, incl pull-throughs; showers, dump station, playground, spray park. Reservable online 90 days out plus some FCFS; prime season late Apr-early Oct, 3 winter pull-thru sites. --Claude

name: Young's Point Provincial Park
note: Provincial park on the north shore of Sturgeon Lake, ~23 km W of Valleyview off Hwy 43; 124 sites across 4 loops (78 with 15/30-amp power, incl the lakeside Big Horn loop; 46 unserviced), showers, dump, boat launch; open ~May–Oct, reservable online. --Claude

name: Smoky River South Provincial Recreation Area
note: 22 unserviced sites plus a day-use area along the Smoky River, 5 km N of Grande Cache on paved Hwy 40; a base for Sulphur Gates canyon and hiking. Vault toilets, bring your own water. First-come, first-served self-registration (cash/cheque), $25/night, open ~May long weekend to Thanksgiving. --Claude

name: Sheep Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small drive-in Alberta Parks PRA campground 25 km north of Grande Cache on Hwy 40; 6 non-serviced open sites along the Smoky River, boat launch, outhouses, no potable water. First-come, first-served ($25/night). Open ~May long weekend to Thanksgiving. --Claude

name: Winagami Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park campground on Winagami Lake, ~25 min from High Prairie; 66 treed sites — 48 powered, 17 unserviced — plus showers/flush toilets, sani-dump, boat launch and piers. Reservable online (90 days ahead); open mid-May to mid-Oct. --Claude
